q: In an organised dogfighting case, wounds are MOST characteristically distributed on which body regions?
o: Dorsal thorax and perianal region
Distal limbs and ventral abdomen
Face/ears, neck/scruff, and medial thighs
Dorsal lumbar region and tail base
e: Organised dogfighting produces a characteristic injury distribution: face and ears (primary bite targets), neck and scruff (grip zone), and medial thighs (exposed when dogs are locked together). This distribution, especially when combined with old scars and fresh wounds at the same sites, is the hallmark finding distinguishing organised fighting from a single dog-fight encounter. Intarapanich et al. (2017) validated this distribution in a systematic study of confirmed fighting dogs.

q: Which piece of equipment found at a property is considered the MOST specific indicator of dogfighting operations?
o: A spring pole attached to a tree
Multiple heavy-gauge tethering chains
A weighted treadmill (carpet mill)
A breaking stick
e: The breaking stick — a wedge-shaped implement used to pry apart locked dog jaws — has no legitimate purpose outside of dogfighting. Carpet mills, spring poles, and tethering chains are used in legitimate dog sports (weight pull, protection sport, hunting). The breaking stick is considered near-definitive evidence of dogfighting operations and is the single most specific item.

q: An adult rooster has a flat, scarred crown where the comb once was, and abnormally short natural spurs. This presentation is MOST consistent with:
o: Deliberate dubbing (comb and wattle removal) and spur trimming for cockfighting
Breed-typical appearance of a Silkie or Polish bantam
A genetic mutation causing comb agenesis
Frostbite damage to the comb from cold exposure
e: Dubbing (surgical removal of the comb and wattles) combined with spur trimming (to allow gaff attachment) is the diagnostic combination for a cockfighting bird. Frostbite can damage combs but does not produce the clean scar of deliberate dubbing. Silkies have small crests but normal spurs. The combination of dubbed comb + short natural spur in an adult rooster is the exam-testable sign of a cockfighting bird.

q: Under 7 U.S.C. § 2156 (Animal Welfare Act), which of the following is a federal felony?
o: Owning a dog that has previously been in a fight, even without the owner's knowledge
Attending a dogfight or cockfight as a spectator
Owning a breaking stick without proof of its intended use
Breeding pit bull-type dogs for sale
e: Since 2014, attending a dogfight or cockfight as a spectator is a federal felony under the Animal Welfare Act. This is a specific and testable legal point. Simply owning a dog with a fighting history (without knowledge or intent) is not the same as participating in fighting. Breeding pit bull-type dogs is legal. The breaking stick itself is a physical object — possession is evidence of fighting but the crime requires the fighting activity or intent.

q: Blood recovered from the surface of a fighting pit is submitted for STR profiling. The profile matches a blood sample from Dog #14, one of 30 dogs seized from the property. This result:
o: Is inadmissible because animal DNA evidence cannot be used in criminal proceedings
Identifies the breed of Dog #14, which determines whether fighting charges apply
Establishes that Dog #14's blood was deposited in the fighting pit, supporting the conclusion that the dog was present at the fight location
Proves Dog #14 was forced to fight, establishing intent without other evidence
e: STR profiling links biological material (blood on the pit surface) to a specific individual dog. This is powerful circumstantial evidence that the dog was present at the fight location. It does not, on its own, prove intent or force — but combined with the dog's injury pattern, the scene evidence, and other findings, it substantially strengthens the prosecution's case. Animal DNA evidence is admissible and has been used successfully in US criminal proceedings.

q: When collecting DNA swabs from blood on a breaking stick, the swabs should be stored in:
o: A red-top tube with formalin preservative at 4°C (39.2°F)
A paper envelope or bag, air-dried, with chain-of-custody label
An EDTA tube frozen at −20°C (−4°F)
A sealed plastic bag at room temperature
e: Biological samples for DNA analysis must be air-dried and stored in paper — not plastic. Sealed plastic containers trap moisture, causing bacterial growth and DNA degradation that renders samples useless for profiling. Allow swabs to air-dry completely before placing in paper envelopes. Label with case number, location on the item, date, time, and collector's name. Log when transferred to the lab or law enforcement.

q: Cockfighting became a federal felony in the United States in which year?
e: Cockfighting became a federal felony in 2008 under the Animal Fighting Prohibition Enforcement Act, which was later incorporated into the 2014 Farm Bill. Dogfighting became a federal felony earlier, in 1976. Attending a fight became a federal crime in 2014. These dates are specifically testable on specialty exams.

q: A shelter receives 45 dogs seized from a dogfighting operation. What is the MOST appropriate approach to determining which dogs can be adopted?
o: Conduct individualised, validated behavioural assessments on each dog — fighting history does not determine adoptability
Euthanise all 45 dogs — fighting dogs are irreversibly dog-aggressive and cannot be safely placed
Use breed (pit bull type) as the primary determinant — all pit bulls from fighting operations must be euthanised
Release all dogs to rescue organisations immediately to reduce holding costs
e: The landmark Michael Vick case (2007) established the precedent that dogs from fighting operations require individualised behavioural assessment and should not be blanket euthanised. Many dogs from fighting operations are highly people-oriented. Each dog must receive an individual validated behavioural evaluation. Disposition decisions require court authorisation — releasing animals without court approval is destruction of evidence. Breed alone cannot determine adoptability.

q: A forensic veterinary team examined 50 roosters seized from an illegal cockfighting operation in Brazil, performing live-animal exams (body condition scoring, lesion documentation, photo-documentation) on 49 birds plus a necropsy on the one that died. Which finding was documented in ALL of the live birds examined?
o: Corneal ulceration
Edema and inflammation of the limbs
Emaciation due to starvation
Lesions of the face, neck, wings, and chest
e: Every one of the 49 live roosters examined (100%) showed emaciation due to starvation, making it the single most consistent finding of the forensic exam. Characteristic grooming (87%) and combat-related lesions to the face, neck, wings, and chest (63%) were also common but not universal. Corneal ulcers/facial edema (26%) and limb edema/inflammation (10%) were less frequent, and the necropsy on the bird that died separately documented severe emaciation, pododermatitis, and a foreign body in the crop.
